## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible branchless blend over identity-ordered particles can approach the streaming ceiling without cache-spill knees, with death rate only modestly raising the floor.

## Cache saturation
At N=4000 (past the L1d spill at N≈963, within L2) ns/p is 8.161 at q=0.01 — overhead dominates. Cost FALLS to 5.261 by N=65000 (right at the L2 spill, N≈61680) and stays FLAT through N=4000000 (5.195 ns/p), a 1.3% spread with no knee at the L2→DRAM transition. This flat shape holds at every death rate. Death rate shifts the floor non-monotonically — q=0.01 at ~5.2 ns/p, q=0.05 at ~5.35, q=0.1 at ~5.05, q=0.25 at ~4.7 (fastest), q=0.5 back to ~5.3 — but never alters the N-shape.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 14.54 GB/s at q=0.25, N=262000 — 57.7% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.01 the peak is 13.09 GB/s (51.9%); at q=0.5, 12.82 GB/s (50.8%). The algo is overhead-bound at N=4000 (8.33 GB/s, 33% of ceiling) and transitions to a compute-bound plateau by N=65000 where it holds 50–58% of ceiling regardless of N. It never approaches streaming. Flat ns/p at large N combined with sub-ceiling bandwidth points to instruction throughput, not memory, as the limiter.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the per-particle loop. The hot path (0x10005728c) uses scalar `ldp s4, s5` for two position floats, then scalar `fadd`, `fmul`, `fcvtzs`, `fsub` — one particle at a time. Only 2 vector-suffixed instructions exist: two `uqadd.8b` (0x100057264, 0x100057278) doing 8-byte saturating add in a fast-path pixel update. The general pixel path is byte-granular scatter: repeated `ldrb`/`add`/`csel`/`strb` triples (strb=16, ldrb=13) writing individual R/G/B bytes with branchless clamp via `csel` to 0xff. A `ldr d3, [x12, x14, lsl #3]` gathers from a small lookup table. Heavy `str`/`stp` (77+35) sets up the `bl _halide_b1` call at 0x100057224. Scalar floats and byte scatter explain the 52% ceiling cap.

## Verdict
Partially — no cache-spill knee appears (flat 5.195–5.261 ns/p from N=65000 to N=4000000 at q=0.01), confirming the blend avoids memory-bound degradation. But peak bandwidth is 14.54 GB/s = 57.7% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling (q=0.25, N=262000), capped by scalar-only float math and 16 byte-granular `strb` scatter stores with zero vectorized particle loops. The non-monotonic death-rate response — q=0.25 fastest at 4.675 ns/p, q=0.5 slowest at 5.324 ns/p — contradicts the predicted modest floor raise.
